neureguline-activated receptor heterodimers in Schwann cells are composed of HER2 and HER-3, whereas those in oligodendocytes consist of HER4 and HER2.

the mechanisms by which the axonal neuregulin signal is transduced by glial cells to regulate the myelin sheath.
the molecular and cellular biology of myelin formation and maintenance, and the role of neuropeptides and growth factors in this process.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of myelinated axons and the maintenance of the myelinated internodal segment.

neuregulin signaling through HER4 in oligodendrocites, and through HER2 and 3 in Schwann cells, is essential for the maintenance of the myelinating phenotype.

axon-derived neuregulns activate Schwann cells via HER2:HER2 and HER2:HER 3 heterodimers, and they activate oligodendroglia via HER4.

the neureguline receptor family is a good candidate for a signaling pathway between neurons and oligodendrogia that is required for myelination.
